# Table

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

A table element with support for column weights, cell padding, borders, headers, and footers

Namespace `BonniePDF`. Extends `BorderedElementBase`. Implements `IRoleProvider`, `IStatefulElement`.


### `Presentation`

```csharp
bool Presentation { get; set; }
```

When `true`, the table is a layout (presentation) table: it arranges content in a grid with no tabular data relationships. Per ISO 14289-1 §7.5 / Matterhorn checkpoint 15, such a table MUST NOT be tagged with table structure — so it is tagged as a generic `Div` grouping and each cell's content is tagged with its own natural role in row-major reading order (no `Table`/`THead`/`TR`/`TH`/ `TD`, and `AddHeader`/`IsHeader` are ignored for tagging). Visual output is unchanged. Default `false` (a semantic data table).

### `RunningTotalColumn`

```csharp
int? RunningTotalColumn { get; set; }
```

Turns on a running total: the column (0-based, at least 1) that shows it. When the body breaks across pages, each page that continues ends with a "carried forward" row holding the total of the rows' `RunningValue` so far, and the next page opens, after any repeated header, with a "brought forward" row holding the same total. The label spans the columns before this one. Both rows are drawn in the footer colours and left out of the accessibility structure, since they repeat what the rows already say. Null (the default) turns the feature off.

### `RunningTotalFormat`

```csharp
string RunningTotalFormat { get; set; }
```

Number format of the running total: `G`, `F<n>`, `N<n>` or `P<n>`, as for charts. Default `"N2"`.

### `RunningTotalPrefix`

```csharp
string RunningTotalPrefix { get; set; }
```

Text written before the running total, such as a currency symbol. Default empty.

### `RenderStateful`

```csharp
RenderStatus RenderStateful(RenderContext ctx, float width)
```

Renders this table with state tracking for pagination. Rows that don't fit on the current page will be continued on the next page. Headers repeat on each continuation page if RepeatHeadersOnNewPage is true.
